title: Accurate magnetic characterization based model development for switched reluctance machine

source.citation: M. Hamouda, L. Számel, Periodica Polytechnica Electrical Engineering and Computer Science 63(3), 2019, pp. 202-212

related.citation: IntechOpen chapter by M. Hamouda and L. Számel on the same machine, 2019 (CC BY-NC 4.0)
related.use: Names the FEMM steel of the same model; read, not cached, so not quote-checked.

machine.topology: 8/6 switched reluctance machine, four phases, concentrated coils on salient stator poles, salient rotor
machine.symmetry: Full cross-section with A = 0 on the stator's outer surface, as the paper's FE model. Phase A alone is excited; its coils on opposite poles are in series with opposite polarity.

components_map.part: stator: eight parallel-sided salient poles with coil blocks against their sides
four phases of two series coils, 88 turns each
air between the poles and in the gap

stator_poles.quote: it is a 5 hp, 1500 r/min, 8/6 poles, 4 phases

rotor_poles.quote: it is a 5 hp, 1500 r/min, 8/6 poles, 4 phases

phases.quote: it is a 5 hp, 1500 r/min, 8/6 poles, 4 phases

bore_diameter_mm.note: In the authors' FE model (Fig. 13) this is the rotor diameter; see rotor_diameter_mm.

air_gap_mm.note: Fig. 13 shows 0.35 +/- 0.07 mm between the pole faces.

stator_pole_height_mm.note: Measured from the 96.7 mm diameter: the stator pole roots lie at 48.35 + 29.3 = 77.65 mm, as Fig. 13 shows (77.67 mm).

rotor_pole_height_mm.note: Recorded but not used: Fig. 13 puts the rotor pole roots at 30.85 mm, 17.5 mm below the rotor faces; control rotor-root-from-height builds 18.1 mm.

phase_resistance_ohm.note: Recorded but not used by a static solve. It does not fit 176 turns of the 18 AWG wire Fig. 13 names (about 1.4 ohm in series), so the model's wire label is nominal.

rotor_diameter_mm.reason: Table 1's 96.7 mm 'bore diameter' is the rotor diameter of the authors' FE model: in Fig. 13 the rotor faces lie at 48.375 +/- 0.05 mm radius and the stator faces at 48.72 +/- 0.05 mm, while the stator pole roots (77.67 mm) and the shaft (17.99 mm) sit where Table 1 puts them. The targets are that model's results.
rotor_diameter_mm.note: The conventional reading, a 96.7 mm stator bore and a 95.9 mm rotor, is the control.

rotor_root_radius_mm.figure: Fig. 13, p. 209 (a rendering of the authors' FEMM model at 15 degrees)
rotor_root_radius_mm.scale_reference: Stator outside diameter 179.5 mm (Table 1); the 36 mm shaft checks the scale to 0.07% and all fitted circles share one centre within 0.2 px
rotor_root_radius_mm.note: Circle fitted to the rotor's root arcs in Fig. 13: 30.853 mm. Table 1's 18.1 mm rotor pole height would give 30.25 mm from the 48.35 mm rotor faces (control rotor-root-from-height).

rotor_root_width_mm.figure: Fig. 13, p. 209 (a rendering of the authors' FEMM model at 15 degrees)
rotor_root_width_mm.scale_reference: Stator outside diameter 179.5 mm (Table 1); the 36 mm shaft checks the scale to 0.07% and all fitted circles share one centre within 0.2 px
rotor_root_width_mm.note: Tapered rotor poles: lines fitted to the sides of all six rotor poles in Fig. 13 give a half-width of 9.05 mm at the face corners (the 21.5 degree arc gives 9.02) and 9.77 mm where they meet the 30.85 mm root arcs. Control parallel-rotor-poles.

coil_start_mm.figure: Fig. 13, p. 209 (a rendering of the authors' FEMM model at 15 degrees)
coil_start_mm.scale_reference: Stator outside diameter 179.5 mm (Table 1); the 36 mm shaft checks the scale to 0.07% and all fitted circles share one centre within 0.2 px
coil_start_mm.note: Inner end of the coil blocks along the pole axis, from the four axis-aligned poles of Fig. 13 (49.36-49.42 mm); the diagonal poles read 49.50-49.53 mm (control coil-blocks-diagonal-reading).

coil_end_mm.figure: Fig. 13, p. 209 (a rendering of the authors' FEMM model at 15 degrees)
coil_end_mm.scale_reference: Stator outside diameter 179.5 mm (Table 1); the 36 mm shaft checks the scale to 0.07% and all fitted circles share one centre within 0.2 px
coil_end_mm.note: Outer end of the coil blocks, axis-aligned poles 72.83-72.89 mm; diagonal poles 72.96-73.00 mm.

coil_outer_offset_mm.figure: Fig. 13, p. 209 (a rendering of the authors' FEMM model at 15 degrees)
coil_outer_offset_mm.scale_reference: Stator outside diameter 179.5 mm (Table 1); the 36 mm shaft checks the scale to 0.07% and all fitted circles share one centre within 0.2 px
coil_outer_offset_mm.note: Distance of the coil blocks' outer edge from the pole axis, axis-aligned poles 17.47-17.49 mm; diagonal poles 17.23-17.27 mm. The blocks' inner edges lie on the pole sides.

steel_grade.value: Cold rolled low carbon strip steel
steel_grade.reason: Fig. 13 labels the iron only 'Steel'. The authors' companion chapter on the same FEMM model (M. Hamouda, L. Szamel, IntechOpen 2019, doi:10.5772/intechopen.89851) names FEMM's 'cold rolled low carbon strip steel'; that source is not cached here, so the name is an assumption with a control.

coil_material.figure: Fig. 13, p. 209 (a rendering of the authors' FEMM model at 15 degrees)
coil_material.note: The coil blocks' material label in Fig. 13; magnet wire with unit permeability, so it does not affect a static solve.

shaft_material.figure: Fig. 13, p. 209 (a rendering of the authors' FEMM model at 15 degrees)

face_max_segment_deg.reason: Pole-face arcs in 0.21 mm segments, so about two element layers cross the 0.4 mm gap.

air_mesh_mm.reason: Air between the poles; the gap is refined by the face arcs.

stator_face_half_width_mm.note: Parallel stator pole sides: Fig. 13's sides lie 8.62-8.67 mm from the pole axes all along the poles.

gaps.item: what Table 1's 96.7 mm bore diameter measures
gaps.affects: the rotor diameter, the rotor pole height and the unaligned air path
gaps.note: The rotor diameter, as the authors' FE model in Fig. 13 shows; control table-bore-reading builds the conventional reading.

gaps.item: rotor pole root and side shape
gaps.affects: unaligned and partly aligned flux linkage
gaps.note: From Fig. 13: root arcs at 30.85 mm (not the 30.25 mm Table 1's pole height implies) and sides tapering from 18.1 to 19.55 mm; controls rotor-root-from-height and parallel-rotor-poles.
Rectangular blocks against the pole sides from Fig. 13; control coil-blocks-diagonal-reading.

gaps.item: series or parallel coils, and whether Fig. 8 is a pole's or the phase's flux linkage
gaps.note: The phase's, with its two 88-turn coils in series: Fig. 13 places both coils in circuit A with ±88 turns, and the aligned 0.877 Wb at 18 A means 1.9 T in a stator pole over 176 turns; a single pole's 88 turns would need 3.8 T.
FEMM's cold rolled low carbon strip steel, as the companion chapter names; control steel-hot-rolled.
The paper's FEM neglects end windings; so does the 2D model. Measured curves are comparators only.

controls.purpose: Every explicit mesh size and arc segment at 0.6 times, about three element layers across the gap.
The conventional reading of Table 1: a 96.7 mm stator bore, a 95.9 mm rotor and an 18.1 mm rotor pole height.
Rotor pole roots 18.1 mm below the rotor faces, as Table 1's pole height, instead of Fig. 13's 30.85 mm.
Parallel-sided rotor poles instead of Fig. 13's taper.
The coil blocks as read on Fig. 13's diagonal poles.
Another Metals Handbook low-carbon steel from the FEMM library.

A 5% longer air gap. Added after the first run to investigate the aligned excess: it shows the signature a gap difference leaves (a larger change at low current than in saturation), against the excess's constant ratio across current.

coverage.reproduced: Phase flux linkage against current at the five rotor positions of Fig. 8 (the FEM curves as targets, the measured ones as comparators), and FEM static torque at 15 and 20 degrees (Fig. 10) as comparators. Mutual flux linkages of phases B to D are recorded.
coverage.not_reproduced: The inductance curves of Fig. 9 beyond flux linkage over current, the mutual inductance curves of Fig. 14, the search-coil and LCR measurements, and the dynamic simulations and measured waveforms of Figs. 15-21.

geometry_checks.quantity: stator outer radius (mm), the scale reference
geometry_checks.note: Fig. 13 scaled so its outer circle is 179.5 mm across: 10.44 px per mm.
Table 1 read conventionally gives 48.35 mm (control table-bore-reading).
Table 1's 18.1 mm pole height gives 30.25 mm from the model's rotor faces, 29.85 mm under the conventional reading.

geometry_checks.quantity: stator pole half-width along the pole (mm)
geometry_checks.note: Lines fitted to the sides of the eight stator poles: 8.62-8.67 mm, slope below 0.003.

geometry_checks.quantity: rotor pole half-width at the face and root corners (mm)
geometry_checks.note: Lines fitted to the sides of the six rotor poles; side-to-side spread +/-0.07 mm.

geometry_checks.quantity: coil block: start, end and outer edge (mm)
geometry_checks.note: Axis-aligned poles; the diagonal poles read [49.51, 72.97, 17.25].

geometry_checks.quantity: coil area (mm^2) and copper fill of 88 turns of 18 AWG
geometry_checks.note: The 0.642 ohm phase resistance would need thicker wire (about 15 AWG, fill near 0.7); a static solve does not depend on it.

findings: Unaligned and partly aligned flux linkage pass: at 0 degrees the model is within 0.0003 Wb (0.2%) of the paper's FEM at every current, and at 10 degrees within 0.0043 Wb (1.2%). Nine of the 20 acceptance targets pass: all at 0 and 10 degrees, and 15 degrees at 6 A.

Where the poles overlap the model is high: by 0.012-0.013 Wb at 15 degrees (10-18 A), 0.015-0.024 Wb at 20 degrees and 0.026-0.036 Wb aligned, against a 0.01 Wb tolerance. The excess is a ratio constant across current: the paper's FEM is 1.000, 0.989, 0.973, 0.967 and 0.961 times the model at 0, 10, 15, 20 and 30 degrees, varying by at most 0.7% between 4 A (unsaturated) and 18 A (saturated), and by 0.24% aligned. Fig. 9 confirms the paper's value independently: 105.3 mH aligned at 6 A, against 105.2 mH from Fig. 8 and the model's 109.5 mH.
The mesh is converged: at 0.6 times the mesh (134,000 elements against 62,000) flux linkage moves by at most +0.34% (+0.03% aligned), away from the paper.

No varied input explains the excess, because each leaves a different signature. The conventional reading of Table 1 lowers aligned flux linkage 0.8% and raises the unaligned 1.25%; Table 1's rotor pole height, parallel rotor poles and the other coil reading move aligned values by under 0.9%. A 5% longer air gap lowers aligned flux linkage 4.0% at 2 A but 0.24% at 18 A, and the hot-rolled steel raises it 8.8% at 2 A and 0.4% at 18 A: a gap or a material changes where the curves bend, while the paper's curves have the model's shape, scaled by an amount that depends on position only. A diagnostic outside the case (probes of the vector potential across pole A in a scratch copy) rules out a pole-flux evaluation: 2 x 88 times the flux through the pole near its face is 0.58 of the circuit linkage unaligned, where the paper agrees with the circuit linkage. The cause stays open; the case keeps its inputs and records the eleven failures as reviewed.

The unaligned agreement supports the reading of Fig. 13: 0.2% with the figure's rotor diameter, root radius and pole taper, against +1.25% with the conventional reading of Table 1 and -0.9% with parallel rotor poles.

Measured comparators: the model is 16% below the measured flux linkage unaligned, where end effects (absent in 2D, as in the paper's FEM) are largest, and 3-6% above it aligned; the paper's FEM shows the same pattern with a smaller aligned excess.

Torque comparators: the model's static torque is 6.0-7.1% above Fig. 10 at 15 degrees and 6.4-6.9% at 20 degrees from 8 to 18 A (more at 2-6 A, where the curves are small), consistent with the higher flux linkage where the poles overlap.
Mutual flux linkage: the neighbouring phase B links up to 0.046 Wb at 18 A, 6% of phase A's, and the opposite phase C under 0.003 Wb; Fig. 14 calls the mutuals small (not digitized).

Digitization: Fig. 8's frame lies above its 0.9 Wb gridline, so calibrating on the frame would have read every value 2.2% low. Calibrated on all gridlines (misfit under 0.001 Wb), the readings agree across line and quadratic fits and three windows within 0.001 Wb; the stated uncertainty is 0.005 Wb.
Runs reproduce bit for bit: three runs of the article level and two of each frozen control gave identical values.
retrospective: Longest: the geometry, read from the authors' FE rendering (Fig. 13) by fitting circles and lines at the scale of the stator diameter, which showed Table 1's bore diameter as the rotor's; then the axis calibration of Fig. 8, and the investigation of the aligned excess.

Added generically because this paper needed them: salient_poles (stator or rotor, parallel or tapered, arc or flat roots, coil blocks sharing the pole sides), salient_pole_winding (phase by pole, polarity alternating between a phase's poles or given per pole), digitized targets with an absolute uncertainty, and reviewed failures bound to both tolerance kinds.

Work tools that should move into the brain: a figure digitizer (gridline calibration, curve tracking with local fits, counting stacked curves) and an overlay of a built model on a paper's rendering at a fitted scale. All three development papers so far needed figure readings.
Skill proposal: let quotes come from cached related sources, so a fact a companion source states (here the chapter naming the steel) can be quoted rather than assumed.

Lessons added: calibrate plot axes on gridlines; a rendering of the authors' FE model shows what they solved; read a discrepancy's signature across current before blaming an input; how salient-pole machines are built.
